cases.sentence: Я выскочил на ___, устланную мокрой брусчаткой.
cases.explain: «На» with a verb of motion («выскочил») answers «куда?» and takes the accusative; площадь is a feminine noun in -ь, whose accusative looks like the nominative.

cases.sentence: Он часто ночевал там при свете ___.
cases.explain: «Свет» governs the thing giving light in the genitive — свет костра — the ordinary noun-plus-noun possessive link.

cases.sentence: Кремль сиял передо мной во всем ___.
cases.explain: The fixed phrase «во всём …» uses «в» in its static sense, which requires the prepositional case.
The instrumental names the means or cause by which a state comes about, so «извелся» is followed by страхом.
«Сделать» takes the person affected in the dative — the indirect object of the action.

cases.sentence: Мне не нужна ___, мне нужен покой.
cases.explain: With «нужен/нужна» the thing needed is the grammatical subject and stands in the nominative, while the person needing it goes into the dative (мне).

cases.sentence: Я в поисках ___ всегда натыкался на Курский вокзал.
cases.explain: The noun «поиски» takes the thing sought in the genitive: в поисках Кремля.

reading.question: What does Venichka conclude once he has run out onto the square and caught his breath?
options: That this place is not Petushki
That he has finally reached Petushki
That he is back at the Kursk station
reading.correct: That this place is not Petushki
reading.explain: He looks around, gets his breath back, and rules out the idea that the town could be Petushki.

reading.question: What does Venichka say about the Lord and Petushki?
options: That the Lord did not pass Petushki by
That the Lord had never heard of Petushki
That the Lord lived in Petushki all his life
reading.correct: That the Lord did not pass Petushki by
reading.explain: His argument that this cannot be Petushki rests on the claim that the Lord skirted this place, whereas Petushki He did not avoid.

reading.ru: Пламени не надо, был бы хоть пепел и дым.
reading.question: What does Venichka say would be enough for him?
options: Just the ashes and the smoke, without the flame
A full fire burning all night
The light of the street lamps
reading.correct: Just the ashes and the smoke, without the flame
reading.explain: He says he found traces of the Lord's overnight stops in the souls of Petushki, and that ashes and smoke alone would satisfy him.

reading.ru: Кремль сиял передо мной во всем великолепии.
reading.question: What does Venichka finally see in front of him?
options: The Kremlin, shining in all its splendour
The monument to Minin and Pozharsky
reading.correct: The Kremlin, shining in all its splendour
reading.explain: After a lifetime of never finding it, the Kremlin appears before him at this moment.

reading.ru: И вот теперь наконец увидел – когда Курский вокзал мне нужнее всего на свете!..
reading.question: Why is the sight of the Kremlin bitterly ironic for Venichka here?
options: He sees it exactly when he needs the Kursk station most of all
He sees it just after buying his ticket to Petushki
He sees it only in a dream and not in reality
He sees it but cannot remember its name
reading.correct: He sees it exactly when he needs the Kursk station most of all
reading.explain: He had always looked for the Kremlin and hit the Kursk station instead; now the Kremlin appears at the one moment the station is what he needs.

reading.ru: Топот все приближался – а я уже ничего не мог.
reading.question: What state is Venichka in as the sound of the pursuit gets closer?
options: He is running faster than ever
He is calmly waiting for them
He has hidden and cannot be seen
reading.explain: The tramping feet come nearer while his own strength gives out.

reading.ru: Я, спотыкаясь, добрел до Кремлевской стены – и рухнул.
reading.question: Where does Venichka collapse?
options: On the steps of a stranger's entrance hall
At the monument to Minin and Pozharsky
On the platform of the Kursk station
reading.explain: He stumbles as far as the Kremlin wall and falls there.

reading.ru: Мне не нужна дрожь, мне нужен покой, – вот все мои желания.
reading.question: What does Venichka say is the whole of what he wants?
options: To see the Kremlin once more
reading.explain: Lying by the wall he says he does not need the shaking, only peace — that is all he desires.

reading.ru: Они приближались с четырех сторон, поодиночке.
reading.question: How do the pursuers close in on Venichka?
options: From four sides, one by one
In a single line from the front
In a car driving across the square
reading.correct: From four sides, one by one
reading.explain: They come at him separately from four directions, then surround him breathing heavily.

reading.question: What is shouted during the beating?
options: To kick him in the belly with a boot
To let him get up off the ground
To take him to the Kursk station
reading.correct: To kick him in the belly with a boot
reading.explain: One of the attackers urges another to boot him in the stomach so that he writhes.

reading.ru: Где Курский вокзал и куда бежать?
reading.question: What is Venichka trying to work out during his brief stop at the monument?
options: Where the Kursk station is and which way to run
Which of the two statues is Minin
Whether the pursuers have given up
How much money he has left
reading.correct: Where the Kursk station is and which way to run
reading.explain: He wipes the blood off his brows to see better and asks himself which direction to take; with no time to think, he runs where Prince Pozharsky is pointing his gaze.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that, if the Lord left this earth for good, He has never once looked in this direction?
sentences: Я выскочил на площадь, устланную мокрой брусчаткой, оглянулся и перевел дух.
Если Он навсегда покинул мою землю, но видит каждого из нас, – Он в эту сторону ни разу и не взглянул.
А если Он никогда моей земли не покидал, если всю ее исходил босой и в рабском виде, – Он это место обогнул и прошел стороной.
highlight.explain: The third sentence states the first of the two hypotheses, about the Lord who has departed but still sees everyone.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that flame is not needed, so long as there are ashes and smoke?
sentences: Он часто ночевал там при свете костра, и я во многих тамошних душах замечал следы Его ночлега – пепел и дым Его ночлега.
Пламени не надо, был бы хоть пепел и дым.
highlight.explain: The closing sentence of the paragraph is the one that gives up the flame and settles for ashes and smoke.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes Venichka stumbling as far as the Kremlin wall and falling down?
sentences: Топот все приближался – а я уже ничего не мог.
Я, спотыкаясь, добрел до Кремлевской стены – и рухнул.
«Что это за люди и что я сделал этим людям?» – такого вопроса у меня не было, я весь издрог и извелся страхом, мне было все равно.
И заметят они меня или не заметят – тоже все равно.
«Мне не нужна дрожь, мне нужен покой, – вот все мои желания. Пронеси, Господь…»
highlight.explain: Only the second sentence reports the physical act of reaching the wall and collapsing.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes Venichka's head being smashed against the Kremlin wall?
sentences: От нас хотел убежать? – прошипел один и схватил меня за волосы и, сколько в нем было силы, хватил меня головой о кремлевскую стену.
Мне показалось, что я раскололся от боли, кровь стекала по лицу и за шиворот…
highlight.explain: The second sentence carries the attacker's hiss together with the blow of his head against the wall.
